executive_summary: Using only the trustworthy 19-entry Phase 5I-A current-corpus ground truth, computed real Recall@k/MRR for semantic/BM25/hybrid retrieval, diagnosed all 3 misses to exact root cause, and evaluated two improvement candidates offline. Baseline hybrid R@5=84.2%, R@10=89.5%. Hybrid measurably beats semantic-only and BM25-only at every k. All 3 misses diagnosed with concrete stage-by-stage evidence: Miss 1 (EN->EN) is a mild RRF ranking issue (rank 8); Miss 2 (Hinglish->Hindi) is BM25 cross-script failure (raw score literally 0.0); Miss 3 (EN->Hindi) is genuine embedding cross-language weakness, absent from the top-100 pool entirely. The multilingual embedding experiment is the phase's key methodological result: it looked like a clear win in semantic-only isolation (fixed Miss 3, no English regression) but when simulated through the FULL hybrid+RRF pipeline using the same real BM25 rankings, that fix evaporates (Miss 3 remains unresolved) and a new Hindi->Hindi regression appears (100%->66.7%) in a category the current system already handles perfectly. Overall hybrid R@5 unchanged, R@10 worse. This directly demonstrates the exact trap the task warned against. The reranker fixes 2 of 3 misses but introduces a new regression and adds real latency, and cannot help Miss 3 at all (candidate never generated). No production change implemented.

overall_recall_mrr.conclusion: Hybrid outperforms semantic-only at every k, matches-or-beats BM25-only at every k - BM25 is genuinely useful on this dataset

full_hybrid_simulated_result.method: New semantic rankings fused with the SAME real captured BM25 rankings via the real, unmodified reciprocal_rank_fusion(), no Qdrant writes
full_hybrid_simulated_result.mechanism: Multilingual model's own semantic rank for Miss 3 improved dramatically (180->3) but BM25's independent rank for the same chunk stayed poor (127, unaffected by embedding model); RRF fusion of one strong + one weak signal was not enough to overcome the weak leg. Two of three genuine Hindi->Hindi cases got measurably worse semantic rankings under the new model.

multilingual_embedding_experiment.conclusion: Category C - NO SAFE IMPROVEMENT FOUND, based on rigorous full-pipeline-simulated evidence, not the misleading isolated-language signal. Directly demonstrates why the task's explicit warning against concluding from single-language improvement was necessary.

rrf_analysis: Confirmed directly in miss analysis and multilingual simulation: RRF's equal-weighting of two independently-ranked legs means a genuine improvement in one leg can be substantially or fully neutralized when the other leg still performs poorly for the same case. No alternative RRF weighting or pool-size scheme implemented, per instruction not to implement candidates yet - documented as an architectural observation for future evaluation.

security_isolation_impact: Not independently re-tested this phase - no code affecting HybridRetriever's workspace/document filtering, ConversationManager, or Phase 5F/5G injection-defense code was touched. All retrieval scoped per-entry by ground truth's own workspace_id using the real, unmodified filtering path. No new isolation risk since no production code changed.
exact_recommended_next_step: 1. If the reranker is seriously considered: needs a larger ground truth (19 entries too small to be confident the one regression isn't representative), latency testing under realistic concurrent load, and a generation-quality check (not just Recall@k)

2. Do not pursue this specific multilingual embedding model further without first addressing BM25's demonstrated inability to bridge cross-script queries - any future embedding experiment should be evaluated the same rigorous full-hybrid-simulated way from the start

3. Investigate whether BM25's script-mismatch failure could be addressed by a language-agnostic, non-model-migration change (e.g. transliteration-aware tokenization) as a potentially more targeted fix - not evaluated this phase, flagged as a direction only

4. Expand the ground truth, particularly Hindi-source-content diversity (only 5/19 entries involve Hindi source, only 2 involve genuine cross-language directions) before drawing further quantitative cross-language conclusions
